title: Sites

static.name: Static
static.description: HTML, CSS and JavaScript files served as they are.

php.name: PHP
php.description: A PHP application with a PHP-FPM pool of its own.

proxy.name: Reverse proxy
proxy.description: Forwards requests to an application listening elsewhere.

app.name: App (Node.js / Python / Go / Java / .NET)
app.description: A long-running program, run as a service behind nginx.

list.hint: Select a domain to open its settings

create.title: New site
create.description: Each site gets its own directory under /srv/www and two system users.
create.httpsLater: No valid certificate covers these domains yet. Once the site exists, issue one from its HTTPS settings.

delete.title: Delete site {site}?
delete.text: The web server configuration of {site} is removed, so its domains are no longer served.
delete.files: Also delete the files and users
delete.filesOn: {dir} and the users {owner} and {runner} are deleted. This cannot be undone.
delete.filesOff: {dir} and the site’s users are kept, so the files are still there if you create the site again.

empty.title: No sites yet
empty.text: A site serves one or more domains from this server: static files, a PHP application with a PHP-FPM pool of its own, or a reverse proxy to an application. Each site gets its own directory and users.
empty.nginxText: Sites are served by nginx. Install it on the software page first.

unsupported.selinux: Sites are not available on this system yet (SELinux support is being verified).

statusUnavailable: The panel could not check whether nginx and PHP are installed.
nginxMissing: nginx is not installed, so sites cannot be created yet.
installNginx: Install nginx on the software page
nginxStopped: nginx is installed but not running.

form.domainsHint: Press Enter after each domain. Wildcards (*.example.com) and IPv4 addresses work; international names are converted automatically. No ports.
form.codeHint: A short name for the site directory and users, fixed once the site exists. Leave it empty to derive it from the first domain; it cannot end in “-run”.
form.webSocketHint: Pass WebSocket connections through to the upstream.
form.upstreamHostHint: The upstream receives its own host name instead of the domain the visitor asked for.
form.noPhp: No PHP version with PHP-FPM is installed.
form.installPhp: Install PHP on the software page
form.rootHint: Relative to the site directory, for example public for Laravel. Leave it empty to serve the directory itself.
form.indexHint: File names tried when a directory is requested. Leave empty for the defaults.
form.writableHint: Directories the site may write to, relative to the site directory (uploads, caches). Everything else stays read-only to it.
form.certHint: Only valid certificates that cover every domain of the site are listed.
form.certNotCovering: The certificate does not cover every domain of the site.
form.redirectHint: Visitors who come over HTTP are sent to HTTPS.
form.hstsHint: Browsers then refuse plain HTTP for this site for a long time, even if HTTPS is turned off later. Turn it on only when HTTPS is meant to stay.
form.proxyHint: http(s)://host[:port][/path], for example an app listening on this server.

settings.applying: A change is being applied; the next one can be made when it is done.

overview.users: {owner} owns the files; deploy code as this user. The site runs as {runner}, which can read the files but write only the writable directories, so a compromised site cannot change its own code.

drift.title: The last change did not take effect
drift.text: What the system runs differs from these settings.

logs.dropped: Only the newest lines are kept on the page.

rewrite.intro: Built-in rules for common applications. Custom rules are not available yet.
rewrite.noneHint: Requests are served from files only.

app.runtimeHint: Installed runtimes only; the chosen one comes first on PATH.
app.installRuntime: Install a runtime on the software page
app.commandHint: One shell line, run by /bin/sh as the site's runtime user. The app must listen on 127.0.0.1:$PORT; HOST and PORT are set for it.
app.envHint: HOST, PORT, HOME and PATH are set by the panel. Values are stored in a file only root can read.
app.writableHint: The app can write only these directories and tmp/; everything else is read-only to it.
app.limitsHint: Memory in MB (at least 16); CPU in percent of one CPU (200 = two CPUs, at least 5). Empty means no limit.
app.healthHint: The panel requests this path every 30 seconds. After three failures (no answer, or status 500 or higher) it restarts the app.
app.noSystemd: Needs systemd, which this system does not have.
app.portHintCreate: 1024–65535. Leave it empty to let the panel pick a free port in 20000–29999.
app.portHintEdit: 1024–65535. Leave it empty to keep the current port.
app.workDirHint: Where the command runs, relative to the site directory.
app.noSystemdNotice: Apps run as systemd services. This system has no systemd, so apps cannot be created here.
app.envHiddenHint: Values are shown only to accounts that may manage sites: they often hold passwords and keys.

process.healthFailing: Health check failing ({count} time) | Health check failing ({count} times)

https.offNotice: HTTPS is off: visitors reach the site over plain HTTP.
https.noCertAccess: You cannot see certificates, so the certificate cannot be changed here.
https.noCovering: No valid certificate covers every domain of this site yet.
https.issue: Issue a certificate for these domains
https.issueAnother: Issue another certificate for these domains

backup.intro: Backups are set up as plans on the backups page; one plan can include several sites and databases.
backup.noneText: No backup plan includes this site. Add it to a plan on the backups page.

steps.users: Create the users {owner} (owns the files) and {runner} (runs the site)
steps.php: Create a PHP {version} FPM pool running as {runner}
steps.app: Run the app as a systemd service as {runner}, listening on 127.0.0.1:{port}
steps.appAuto: Run the app as a systemd service as {runner}, on a free port in 20000–29999
steps.nginx: Write the nginx configuration for {domains}, check it with nginx -t and reload nginx

domains.intro: The site answers for these domains; each one must point at this server. The first is the primary domain, shown in lists and opened by “Visit site”.
domains.certNote: The certificate must cover every domain; saving fails for a domain it does not cover.
domains.panelHost: {domains} is also the panel's host name. A browser sends the panel's cookies to every website on the same host name, whatever the port, and such a website can set cookies for the panel. The panel never accepts its cookies alone, but it is safer to keep the panel on a host name of its own, such as panel.example.com. | {domains} are also host names of the panel. A browser sends the panel's cookies to every website on the same host name, whatever the port, and such a website can set cookies for the panel. The panel never accepts its cookies alone, but it is safer to keep the panel on a host name of its own, such as panel.example.com.

php.intro: The site runs in a PHP-FPM pool of its own, as {runner}.

dirs.allowSymlinks: Serve links between the site's own users
dirs.allowSymlinksHint: nginx serves a symbolic link only when the link and the file it points to have the same owner. With this on, each time the site is saved the panel gives a link in the site's directory that points to a file of the site's owner or runtime user the owner of that file, so that links such as Laravel's public/storage are served. Links to other sites' or system files are always refused.
dirs.allowSymlinksRisk: A link made after the site was saved is served once the site is saved again.
